47306-tobias-smollett.creator: Unknown
47306-tobias-smollett.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. ncisive and sympathetic critics that ever pronounced judgment—of the element of inspiration in every great writer of fiction. Experimentally conscious of what was of value in his own case,—himself the great Wizard of Fiction,—he would reason by analogy what would be of power to inspire other men.

arxiv-2204-13699.title: Channel Pruned YOLOv5-based Deep Learning Approach for Rapid and Accurate Outdoor Obstacles Detection
arxiv-2204-13699.creator: Zeqian Li, Yuwei Wang, Kexun Chen, Zhibin Yu
arxiv-2204-13699.description: Abstract One-stage algorithm have been widely used in target detection systems that need to be trained with massive data. Most of them perform well both in real-time and accuracy. However, due to their convolutional structure, they need more computing power and greater memory consumption.

arxiv-2205-04104.title: ReCAB-VAE: Gumbel-Softmax Variational Inference based on Analytic Divergence
arxiv-2205-04104.creator: Sangshin Oh, Seyun Um, Hong-Goo Kang
arxiv-2205-04104.description: Abstract The Gumbel-softmax distribution, or Concrete distribution, is often used to relax the discrete characteristics of a categorical distribution and enable back-propagation through differentiable reparameterization. Although it reliably yields low variance gradients, it still relies on a stochastic sampling process for optimization.

arxiv-2206-10667.title: On the Common Logical Structure of Classical and Quantum Mechanics
arxiv-2206-10667.creator: Andrea Oldofredi, Gabriele Carcassi, Christine A. Aidala
arxiv-2206-10667.description: Abstract At the onset of quantum mechanics, it was argued that the new theory would entail a rejection of classical logic. The main arguments to support this claim come from the non-commutativity of quantum observables, which allegedly would generate a non-distributive lattice of propositions, and from quantum superpositions, which would entail new rules for quantum disjunctions.

arxiv-2301-02697.title: Preferences on Ranked-Choice Ballots
arxiv-2301-02697.creator: Brian Duricy
arxiv-2301-02697.description: Abstract This paper formalizes the lattice structure of the ballot voters cast in a ranked-choice election and the preferences that this structure induces. These preferences are shown to be counter to previous assumptions about the preferences of voters, which indicate that ranked-choice elections require different considerations for voters and candidates alike.

arxiv-2308-15951.title: Aromatic cycles are widespread in cold clouds Thanks: Based on observations carried out with the Yebes 40m telescope (projects 20A016, 21A006, and 22B023). The 40m radio telescope at Yebes Observatory is operated by the Spanish Geographic Institute (IGN; Ministerio de Transportes, Movilidad y Agenda
arxiv-2308-15951.creator: M. Agúndez, N. Marcelino, B. Tercero, J. Cernicharo
arxiv-2308-15951.description: Abstract We report the detection of large hydrocarbon cycles toward several cold dense clouds. We observed four sources (L1495B, Lupus-1A, L483, and L1527) in the Q band (31-50 GHz) using the Yebes 40m radiotelescope. Using the line stack technique, we find statistically significant evidence of benzonitrile (C 6 H 5 CN) in L1495B, Lupus-1A, and L483 at levels of 31.

arxiv-2402-07759.title: Robust and accurate simulations of flows over orography using non-conforming meshes
arxiv-2402-07759.creator: Giuseppe Orlando, Tommaso Benacchio, Luca Bonaventura
arxiv-2402-07759.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Giuseppe Orlando, Tommaso Benacchio, Luca Bonaventura. We systematically validate the static local mesh refinement capabilities of a recently proposed IMEX-DG scheme implemented in the framework of the deal.II library. Non-conforming meshes are employed in atmospheric flow simulations to increase the resolution around complex orography. The proposed approach is fully mass and energy conservative and allows local mesh refinement in the vertical and horizontal direction without relaxation at the internal coarse/fine mesh boundaries.

arxiv-2409-09471.title: Randomized sketched TT-GMRES for linear systems with tensor structure
arxiv-2409-09471.creator: Alberto Bucci, Davide Palitta, Leonardo Robol
arxiv-2409-09471.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Alberto Bucci, Davide Palitta, Leonardo Robol. In the last decade, tensors have shown their potential as valuable tools for various tasks in numerical linear algebra. While most of the research has been focusing on how to compress a given tensor in order to maintain information as well as reducing the storage demand for its allocation, the solution of linear tensor equations is a less explored venue.

arxiv-2505-13666.title: Oort Cloud Ecology. III. The Sun left the parent star cluster shortly after the giant planets formed
arxiv-2505-13666.creator: Simon Portegies Zwart 1 and Shuo Huang 1,2
arxiv-2505-13666.description: Abstract Context. The Sun was born in a clustered environment with ∼ < 10 000 \ {\raise-2.15277pt\hbox{$\mathrel{\mathop{\kern 0.0pt\sim}\limits^{<}}$}}\ 10\,000 other stars ( Portegies Zwart 2009 ; Adams 2010 ; Higuchi & Kokubo 2015 ; Arakawa & Kokubo 2023 ) . Being an isolated star today, the Sun must have left the nest.

arxiv-2508-04656.title: Charged Higgs Signatures at Future Electron-Proton Colliders
arxiv-2508-04656.creator: Baradhwaj Coleppa, Gokul B. Krishna
arxiv-2508-04656.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Baradhwaj Coleppa, Gokul B. Krishna. In this work, we present a detailed collider phenomenology study of the charged Higgs boson within a Beyond the Standard Model (BSM) framework featuring an extended gauge and scalar sector.

arxiv-2509-25111.title: When Simple is Enough: Binary Models Capture Social Complexity in Coupled Human–Environment Systems.
arxiv-2509-25111.creator: Yazdan Babazadeh Maghsoodlo, Madhur Anand, Chris T. Bauch
arxiv-2509-25111.description: Abstract 1 Abstract Models of coupled human–environment systems often face a tradeoff between realism and tractability. Spectrum opinion models, where social preferences vary continuously, offer descriptive richness but are computationally demanding and parameter-heavy. Binary formulations, in contrast, are analytically simpler but raise concerns about whether they can capture key socio–ecological feedbacks.

arxiv-2602-18083.title: COMPARATIVE ASSESSMENT OF MULTIMODAL EARTH OBSERVATION DATA FOR SOIL MOISTURE ESTIMATION
arxiv-2602-18083.creator: Ioannis Kontogiorgakis, Athanasios Askitopoulos, Iason Tsardanidis*, Dimitrios Bormpoudakis, Ilias Tsoumas, Fotios Balampanis, Charalampos Kontoes, [1em] BEYOND EO Centre, IAASARS, National Observatory of Athens, Athens, Greece
arxiv-2602-18083.description: Abstract Accurate soil moisture (SM) estimation is critical for precision agriculture, water resources management and climate monitoring. Yet, existing satellite SM products are too coarse ( > > 1 km) for farm-level applications. We present a high-resolution (10 m) SM estimation framework for vegetated areas across Europe, combining Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical imagery and ERA-5 reanalysis data through machine learning.

europmc-pmc5119954.creator: Chen L, Ge B, Casale FP, Vasquez L, Kwan T, Garrido-Martín D, Watt S, Yan Y, Kundu K, Ecker S, Datta A, Richardson D, Burden F, Mead D, Mann AL, Fernandez JM, Rowlston S, Wilder SP, Farrow S, Shao X, Lambourne JJ, Redensek A, Albers CA, Amstislavskiy V, Ashford S, Berentsen K, Bomba L, Bourque G, Bujold D, Busche S, Caron M, Chen SH, Cheung W, Delaneau O, Dermitzakis ET, Elding H, Colgiu I, Bagger FO, Flicek P, Habibi E, Iotchkova V, Janssen-Megens E, Kim B, Lehrach H, Lowy E, Mandoli A, Matarese F, Maurano MT, Morris JA, Pancaldi V, Pourfarzad F, Rehnstrom K, Rendon A, Risch T, Sharifi N, Simon MM, Sultan M, Valencia A, Walter K, Wang SY, Frontini M, Antonarakis SE, Clarke L, Yaspo ML, Beck S, Guigo R, Rico D, Martens JHA, Ouwehand WH, Kuijpers TW, Paul DS, Stunnenberg HG, Stegle O, Downes K, Pastinen T, Soranzo N.

We carried out high-resolution genetic, epigenetic, and transcriptomic profiling in three major human immune cell types (CD14

pmc-10574653.title: Characterization of the Isocitrate Dehydrogenase Gene Family and Their Response to Drought Stress in Maize
pmc-10574653.creator: Ningning Wei, Ziran Zhang, Haoxiang Yang, Die Hu, Ying Wu, Jiquan Xue, Dongwei Guo, Shutu Xu, Fangpu Han
pmc-10574653.description: Isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) is a key rate-limiting enzyme in the tricarboxylic acid cycle and acts in glutamine synthesis. IDH also participates in plant growth and development and in response to abiotic stresses. We identified 11 maize IDH genes (ZmIDH) and classified these genes into ZmNAD-IDH and ZmNADP-IDH groups based on their different coenzymes (NAD+ or NADP+).

pmc-10575041.title: Vascular Plant Species Inventory of Mexico’s Revillagigedo National Park: Awareness of Alien Invaders as a Sine Qua Non Prerequisite for Island Conservation
pmc-10575041.creator: Alejandra Domínguez-Meneses, Juan Esteban Martínez-Gómez, Teresa Mejía-Saulés, Israel Acosta-Rosado, Stefan Stadler
pmc-10575041.description: The Revillagigedo Archipelago, located in the Eastern Pacific Ocean, stands out for its unique biological richness and endemism. These islands remained uninhabited until the second half of the twentieth century, allowing a better conservation status than on other oceanic islands.

pmc-10596086.title: Cost-effectiveness analysis of child eye health interventions in India
pmc-10596086.creator: S Mannava, B R Shamanna
pmc-10596086.description: BackgroundIndia has 4.8 million blind persons including 250,000 blind children, and 35 million visually impaired individuals. Prevalence of blindness is 0.36%, it was 1% two decades ago due to significant public health programs towards prevention and treatment by various stakeholders. Time is opportune for cost-effectiveness analyses of these programs.

pmc-11195767.title: Normal values for native T1 at 1.5 T in the pericardial fluid of healthy volunteers
pmc-11195767.creator: Simon Thalén, Joao G Ramos, Henrik Engblom, Andreas Sigfridsson, Peder Sörensson, Martin Ugander
pmc-11195767.description: AimsT1 mapping cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging has been used to characterize pericardial effusions. The aim of this study was to measure pericardial fluid native T1 values in healthy volunteers to establish normal values.Methods and resultsProspectively recruited volunteers (n = 30) underwent CMR at 1.

pmc-11403868.title: Reduced positive attentional bias in patients with borderline personality disorder compared with non-patients: results from a free-viewing eye-tracking study
pmc-11403868.creator: Taavi Wenk, Anna-Christina Günther, Carolin Webelhorst, Anette Kersting, Charlott Maria Bodenschatz, Thomas Suslow
pmc-11403868.description: BackgroundAttentional processes are important for regulating emotional states and coping with stressful events. Orientation of attention acts as filter for subsequent information processing. So far, only few eye-tracking studies have examined attentional processes during emotion perception in borderline personality disorder (BPD). In these studies, gaze behaviour was analysed during simultaneous or delayed evaluation of single stimuli.

pmc-11511103.title: Unraveling the Secrets of Early-Maturity and Short-Duration Bread Wheat in Unpredictable Environments
pmc-11511103.creator: Charan Singh, Sapna Yadav, Vikrant Khare, Vikas Gupta, Umesh R Kamble, Om P Gupta, Ravindra Kumar, Pawan Saini, Rakesh K Bairwa, Rinki Khobra, Sonia Sheoran, Satish Kumar, Ankita K Kurhade, Chandra N Mishra, Arun Gupta, Bhudeva S Tyagi, Om P Ahlawat, Gyanendra Singh, Ratan Tiwari, Wenshan Guo, Jinfe
pmc-11511103.description: In response to the escalating challenges posed by unpredictable environmental conditions, the pursuit of early maturation in bread wheat has emerged as a paramount research endeavor. This comprehensive review delves into the multifaceted landscape of strategies and implications surrounding the unlocking of early maturation in bread wheat varieties.

pmc-11691335.title: TRACING THE FOOTSTEPS OF THE SCHOLARS FROM DE TORNYAY CENTER FOR HEALTHY AGING AT UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON
pmc-11691335.creator: Yanjing Liang, Priscilla Carmiol-Rodriguez, Sarah McKiddy, Paige Bartlett, Heather Wicklein Sanchez, Basia Belza
pmc-11691335.description: The de Tornyay Center for Healthy Aging has been pivotal in advancing research, education, and practice since 1998. The center faculty has mentored over 165 students, connected them to community partners, awarded them over $757,000 in research funding, and supported the dissemination of their work through travel scholarships.

pmc-12468381.title: Developing and Validating a Childhood Trauma-Informed Curriculum for Primary School Teachers in Limpopo Province, South Africa
pmc-12468381.creator: Muimeleli Munyadziwa, Lufuno Makhado, Piero Pavone
pmc-12468381.description: Highlights What are the main findings? Primary school teachers in rural Limpopo have limited knowledge and training on childhood trauma, affecting their ability to support trauma-exposed learners.The developed trauma-informed curriculum addresses gaps in awareness, early identification of trauma, and classroom strategies to create supportive learning environments. What is the implication of the main finding?

pmc-12837613.title: Cinnamomum cassia Modulates Key Players of Gut–Liver Axis in Murine Lupus
pmc-12837613.creator: Georges Maalouly, Tarek Itani, Nassim Fares
pmc-12837613.description: Background: Systemic lupus erythematosus is a multi-faceted auto-immune disease. Growing evidence points to gut permeability and microbiota as key players in the development of the disease. Cinnamomum cassia is gaining attention as a potential modifier of the gut and liver health.

pmc-12848004.title: Chromosome-scale genome assembly of Flemingia macrophylla
pmc-12848004.creator: Ting Yuan, Xiangyu Wang, Ying Liang, Ying Hu, Yunfang Zhang, Baoyou Huang, Lingyun Chen, Kunhua Wei
pmc-12848004.description: Flemingia macrophylla, a perennial shrub of the family Fabaceae, possesses pharmacological properties such as anti-inflammatory and antibacterial activities. However, its whole genome has remained largely unexplored. In this study, we generated a chromosome-level genome assembly of F. macrophylla by integrating high-fidelity (HiFi) long-read sequencing generated by Pacific Biosciences (PacBio) and high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) scaffolding.

pmc-12876131.title: VEGF-A isoforms induce the expression of APLN in endothelial cells during human prenatal lung development
pmc-12876131.creator: Antony Hoarau, Andrew Frauenpreis, Randa Belgacemi, Emma Loeffler, Osshaya Maalouf, Ian A. Glass, Denise Al Alam, Soula Danopoulos
pmc-12876131.description: IntroductionSingle-cell RNA-sequencing analyses have revealed the existence of two distinct capillary cell populations in the human lung: general capillary cells (CAP1) and alveolar capillary cells (CAP2). Studies in mouse have shown that the splicing of Vegf-a evolves during embryonic development, creating a temporal pattern of expression for different isoforms, which contributes to the formation of pulmonary capillaries.

pmc-13209242.title: Simulation Effect and Mechanism of High-Polymeric Persimmon Tannin on Simulating Alternate-Day Fasting on Regulating Lipid Metabolism in Obese Mice
pmc-13209242.creator: Yajie Zhang, Yunfei Huang, Yawei Xu, Chunmei Li
pmc-13209242.description: Background/Objectives: Obesity represents a significant global health challenge. Although alternate-day fasting (ADF) has been shown to effectively improve metabolic parameters, long-term adherence to this regimen remains limited. This study aimed to investigate whether highly polymerized persimmon tannin (DP31) could serve as a practical alternative to ADF for the prevention of high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity in mice.

pmc-13212563.title: A lightweight hybrid attention network with multi-scale feature integration for intelligent recognition of underwater acoustic targets
pmc-13212563.creator: Nahid-Al Mahmud, Tao Zhang, Yasir Iqbal, Farhana Bari Sumona, Anjum Iqbal, Yanzhang Geng, Wajid Khan, Basem Abu Zneid, Ievgen Zaitsev
pmc-13212563.description: Underwater Acoustic Target Recognition (UATR) plays a significant role in intelligent sonar and underwater environmental monitoring systems, but successful recognition in underwater environments of complex scenarios is a significant challenge because of the effects of ambient noise, signal attenuation, and dynamic propagation.

pmc-13374744.title: Practical guide to implementing pre-emptive pharmacogenetic screening in routine pediatric oncology care
pmc-13374744.creator: Emma C Bernsen, Lidwien M Hanff, Theodorus W Kouwenberg, Melanie M Hagleitner, Bastiaan B J Tops, Nienke Biesot, Jayne Y Hehir-Kwa, Alwin D R Huitema, Meta H M Diekstra
pmc-13374744.description: Interindividual variability in drug response is a challenge in pediatric oncology, where the risk of treatment-related toxicity is exacerbated by narrow therapeutic windows and combination therapies. Pharmacogenetics (PGx) aims to reduce this variability by linking genetic variants to differences in drug pharmacokinetics, efficacy, and toxicity.

pmc-13429620.title: Federated multi-cloud task scheduling with load balancing using multi-objective NSGA-II and reinforcement learning
pmc-13429620.creator: Wad Ghaban, Hind Salem Alatawi
pmc-13429620.description: Task scheduling in federated multi-cloud environments is challenging owing to heterogeneous service-level agreements, decentralized resource control, and dynamic workload characteristics. The existing hybrid optimization approaches lack real-time adaptability across cloud providers also assumes centralized coordination. To work with these issues, this paper proposes Multi-Objective Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm with Q-Learning (MO-NSGAQ).

pmc-13626519.title: Fluoroscopy-guided intrathecal lumbar drain placement in severe post-polio spinal deformity: A case report
pmc-13626519.creator: Shivakumar M. Channabasappa, S Srihari, S Kavyashree, Pooja Shah
pmc-13626519.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Spontaneous cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) rhinorrhoea undergoing endoscopic endonasal repair often requires intraoperative intrathecal lumbar drain (ITLD) placement for fluorescein-assisted fistula localisation and postoperative CSF diversion. Severe spinal deformity can render conventional landmark and ultrasound-guided neuraxial access impossible. We describe a 45-year-old female with post-polio thoracolumbar scoliosis and vertebral rotation undergoing endoscopic repair of a cribriform plate CSF leak, in whom both landmark and ultrasound-guided ITLD placement failed because of absent acoustic windows.
